sources.title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context

cases.question: Under which conditions does attention reduce sequential computation, and what limitations or counterevidence qualify that claim?
cases.scope: Attention Is All You Need and directly related original papers about sequential computation and long-sequence cost.

requirements.criterion: Explain constant sequential operations per self-attention layer, compared with recurrent sequence dependency; distinguish parallel training from generation.
Retain the autoregressive decoder condition: previously generated symbols are inputs when generating the next symbol. Do not infer constant-time full-sequence generation from Table 1.
Report O(n^2 d) full self-attention cost and the n < d comparison condition, rather than claiming universally cheaper attention.
Compare sparse local/global attention as an alternative. State fixed window and bounded global-token assumptions behind linear sequence-length scaling; cite actual observed original evidence.

cases.question: How do later attention methods address long-context cost and context fragmentation, and which restrictions remain?
cases.scope: Original attention mechanisms for long-sequence cost and cross-segment context; compare assumptions rather than benchmark rankings.

requirements.criterion: Identify the quadratic full-attention sequence-length cost.
Explain fixed-length context fragmentation and reuse of previous-segment hidden states with relative positions.
Do not equate beyond fixed-length context with unbounded accessible context: explain depth, segment and cache dependence; distinguish inference speedup evidence from universal asymptotic claims.
Explain the local/global sparse pattern, fixed-window and bounded-global-token conditions, and that it is not unrestricted all-pairs attention.

reviewPolicy: Pre-registered engineering acceptance thresholds, not validated population-level scientific metrics. All claims, required evidence and each round's next action require an independent human review of saved originals. Equivalent observed originals may satisfy a requirement with a justified mapping; their versions must be saved. Missing sources remain omissions. Fixed references are reviewer-only and must not be injected into an open-discovery model prompt.
